key_insight: Chemical bonding remains useful in AI-driven materials science as a learnable representation of electronic structure that can emerge within neural-network embeddings.
engineering_relevance: Explicit bonding descriptors can improve mechanical-property predictions and support more interpretable models for materials discovery.
method: Linearly probe Allegro and MACE embeddings for bonding descriptors.
Add electronic-structure-based bonding features to ESF-MEGNet.
Frame bonding models as compressed electronic information, evaluated by predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity.
evidence_signal: Linear probes recover bonding descriptors with R² > 0.95, while ESF-MEGNet bonding features add information beyond bond distance and reduce prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset coverage or evaluation splits, leaving generalization to unfamiliar materials uncertain.
paper_title: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?
